answer: One concrete defense is a stake-backed reputation vault: each agent locks a small refundable deposit before it can transact, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove fake activity. Above that vault sits a terrace of trust tiers — new agents start on the lowest terrace with tiny limits and climb only through verified, useful work over time. Sybils drown in this design because faking an ocean of identities multiplies the locked stake and the slow climb, making mass forgery cost more than it can ever earn.
